tests.title: Smoothing the stair-steps: anti-aliasing at the full-screen default
tests.when: Now: pick one (read only, no Mac needed). I recommend STP; walk it to check for smearing before it ships.
tests.what: The camera has had no anti-aliasing since full screen went to 2048x1152. All four options keep every room over 30 fps at the default size; 2560x1440 with TAA or SMAA drops the foyer to 27 and the street to 29, so the size stays. Recommendation: STP (temporal, at 100%, no upscale): twigs and railings become continuous lines like TAA but it stays crisper on brick, shingles and wallpaper, for about 4% of the frame. The transparent-pass cost seen before is gone with the room-fitted lamps (switching those passes off changes nothing now).
look: Edges strip (top to bottom): branches against the sky, the blue house's roof and dormer, the newel and balusters, the mirror frame; left to right: none, FXAA, SMAA, TAA, STP, all 2x.
Branches: none and FXAA leave dotted, broken twigs; SMAA cleans the edges but twigs stay broken; TAA and STP draw them whole.
Texture: FXAA blurs the shingles and wallpaper; TAA softens slightly; SMAA and STP keep them.
Still frames can't show smearing in motion (TAA/STP): walk past the banister and the trees before it ships.

tests.title: Night speed: what's expensive in the foyer, kitchen and hall
tests.when: Settled: you kept the lamp range fitted to each room + 1 m (fit=1). It ships in every build from now on (LampFit.cs, applied at load).
tests.what: At the new full-screen default (2048x1152, no dynamic resolution) the night rooms ran 23-29 fps. The biggest win that keeps the look is fitting each lamp's light range to its own room plus 1 m: foyer 23 -> 36, hall 29 -> 45, kitchen 26 -> 32, all over 30. Fog, reflections, ambient occlusion, glass and sheers cost almost nothing. The foyer mirror costs about 20% in the foyer and kitchen. Recommendation: ship 'lamp range fitted to room'.

tests.title: French windows: sheers like the film from the street
tests.when: Now: walk NB9 to the front walk by day and at night.
tests.what: Your request: the ground-floor French windows should show the same sheers as the film. The living room's pair (left of the portico) read as blank cream panels: their sheers hung at the room wall, 0.3 m behind the glass. They now hang on each leaf just behind the glass (film 5650 from inside shows them gathered on the doors; 2508/6399 from outside), same cloth and folds as every other sheer. The dining pair already had them. The leaves don't open, and nothing stands in a walkway. Not changed: the den's bay window at the far left still shows clear glass and the room; in the film it has sheers too. Say if you want it to match.

tests.title: Front brick: upstairs darker than downstairs
tests.when: Premise tests done (Oct 21). Next: the fix above, one bake, on the coordinator's go. Nothing to walk for the brick.
tests.what: NB9 built with probe layers: probes outside the house now stay on (Exterior), rooms Interior, Marina's strip both; outside walls read only outside probes. Result, measured (tools/house/brick_storeys.py, gate 5%): still FAIL. Overcast upstairs/downstairs 0.67 centre, 0.76 wing (NB8 0.71/0.78): the ground floor got brighter (it no longer borrows the rooms' light), the upstairs did not. Night flipped: 1.25/1.31 (NB8 0.63/1.30) because the ground-floor brick lost the warm indoor glow that leaked through it. Sunny 0.92/0.94. Rooms unchanged (foyer and living at night, compared with the lamp fit off). With probes off entirely the upstairs is still 0.81-0.85, so the remaining gap is in the outdoor light upstairs (the eaves, Marina's strip), not the rooms behind. Not shipping as a fix yet; the layers themselves are sound. PREMISE TESTS (Oct 21): (1) Eaves hidden in the live image (roof, cornice, gutters gone): the overcast upstairs barely moves, 0.675 -> 0.691 centre, 0.764 -> 0.778 wing. Not the eaves. (2) ProbeDump read the baked light on a white card in front of each storey: a few tenths of a metre out, the upstairs gets as much outdoor light as downstairs or more (day 34-59 vs 25-28). But right at the upstairs wall face (0-0.15 m) the light drops to 8.5, a quarter of downstairs (23), in the centre; at night the same spot is bright and warm (lamp-lit rooms). Conclusion in plain words: the upstairs darkness is baked in, in the first row of probes at the wall. Those probes sit inside the film's upper wall, but the bake decides which probes count from its LAST pass, Marina's version of the house, which has no wall there. So probes buried in the wall are trusted, and they are dark by day and lamp-lit at night. Proposed fix (one bake): run the film's day bake last, so the wall is there when Unity decides which probes count (or switch those buried probes off with a thin box in the wall). Then re-check the upstairs rooms, which share those probes.
look: Rows 1-3: the upstairs brick is still darker than downstairs by day (FAIL); at night the ground floor is now the darker one.
Rows 4-5: foyer and living at night are unchanged.
Ignore the French windows here; they have their own entry.

Question for you (night sheet): at night the ground-floor brick lost the warm glow it had (centre 62 -> 29). That glow was the rooms' light leaking through the wall. In film 5545 / 10 the plain brick at night is dark red; the warmth on it is spill from the lit windows and the Christmas bulbs. Our reading: NB9's darker ground floor is the more faithful base, and the film's warmth should come from window and bulb spill, not the leak. Do you agree, or do you prefer NB8's look?

tests.title: Full-screen speed: why the Studio Display was slow
tests.what: Lowering the internal resolution (dynamic resolution) was itself the main cost: it stalled the graphics driver for most of each frame. The new default is full screen at a fixed 2048x1152, stretched to the display, with dynamic resolution off; P steps screen sizes. It runs in the next build.
